chapters.title: THREE NUMBERS. SIX CHECKS.
chapters.math: Find a,b,n: positive n; a,b > εn; a!b! ∣ n!k!; C log n < k < C′ log n. Here k = a+b−n.
sentences: Three mystery numbers. Six checks. Can we make every light turn green?
One check means a perfect fit: divide, with nothing left over.

chapters.title: GIVE YOURSELF SOME ROOM.
chapters.math: 0 < C < C′. Choose c = (C+C′)/2, so C < c < C′.
sentences: First, pick a middle setting. Now we've got wiggle room on both sides.

chapters.title: ONE SETTING. FIVE GREEN LIGHTS.
chapters.math: Choose M beyond five eventual thresholds; hM packages the five guarantees.
sentences: Five helpers need a big enough number. Crank it up until every helper is ready.
Now we get the number, plus proof that all five are ready.

chapters.title: THEY CAN'T ALL LOSE.
chapters.math: Counting lemma: |bad| < M+1 = |[M,2M]|. Extract m outside the bad set and its evidence hm.
sentences: The bad candidates get knocked out. But the proof says there aren't enough bad ones to remove everybody.
Someone survives. Take that number, and its proof.

chapters.title: WATCH THE BLUE PIECES.
chapters.code: use m + k_val c M, m, 2 * m;
chapters.math: a=m+k, b=m, n=2m; k=⌊c log M⌋. Thus a+b−n = (m+k)+m−2m = k.
sentences: Build our three numbers from these pieces. Now add the first two and subtract the third.
Blue cancels blue. Again. What's left? Just the yellow piece. That's the gap we needed to control.

chapters.title: BRING THE RECEIPTS.
chapters.math: The construction lemma supplies divisibility and bounds; refine assembles them; linarith/nlinarith finish inequalities.
sentences: Building the numbers isn't enough. Each check needs evidence.
The earlier lemmas bring the receipts. Lean checks every one. Six green lights.

chapters.title: BUILD IT. PROVE IT. DONE.
chapters.math: erdos_728_fc: the proof uses 0<ε<1/2 and 0<C<C′. Standard axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no sorryAx.
sentences: That's the idea: build numbers so the gap becomes simple, then prove every requirement.
